name: Sacré-Cœur
note: The basilica on the summit of Montmartre. Placed on OSM way 23762981's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the porch (−z) facing the city at bearing 175.6, the campanile at +z; the way and its ~45 building:parts (226727320…226727369, whose heights the model follows) are replaced. Named exactly as the skyline stand-in in tools/cities.ts, so the stand-in gives way to it within 1.3 km (render/landmarks.ts `update`). `front` (not rotateDeg, which the skyline code would copy onto the stand-in, whose own frame is long on x while this model is long on z): the same turn, 355.6°, for the model.

name: Panthéon
note: Soufflot's church on the Montagne Sainte-Geneviève. Placed on OSM way 16407465's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the portico (−z) facing the Rue Soufflot at bearing 288.2; the way and its ~75 building:parts (IGN Lidar heights, which the model follows; the portico's 16 mapped columns among them) are replaced. Named exactly as the skyline stand-in in tools/cities.ts, so the stand-in gives way to it within 1.3 km. `front` (not rotateDeg, which the skyline code would copy onto the stand-in, whose own frame is long on x while this model is long on z): the same turn, 108.2°, for the model.

name: Square Louise-Michel — the terraces
note: The stonework of the terraced garden below the basilica: the parvis balustrade (its west run stopping short of the Réservoirs de Montmartre), the fountain's grotto wall, basin and kerb (OSM way 570241111), the candelabra up the central flights. In the basilica's frame moved to basilica-local (1.5, −98), the middle of the stonework; each piece on Fit.groundAt (the square falls ~35 m). The flights themselves are OSM's highway=steps, drawn by the city (render/stairs.ts); the lawns are the park's (way 45189726).

name: Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel
note: Napoleon's arch between the Louvre and the Tuileries. Placed on OSM way 227483542's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), −z toward the Tuileries (bearing 295.7), the axis of the Louvre–Étoile; the way and its 58 building:parts (whose heights the model follows: arches to 9 and 5 m, columns 2–10.5, attic to 16, plinth 17.5) are replaced. The quadriga takes it to ~21.5 m. The building:parts the bake nests under the outline are also named outright (they go with it either way), so the nonbuildings check sees them claimed.

name: Porte Saint-Denis
note: Blondel's gate (1672) astride the Rue Saint-Denis on the boulevard. Placed on OSM relation 3170072's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), −z facing south (bearing 198.2); the arch is open for the street. The building:parts the bake nests under the outline are also named outright (they go with it either way), so the nonbuildings check sees them claimed.

name: Porte Saint-Martin
note: Bullet's gate (1674) astride the Rue Saint-Martin. Placed on OSM relation 3178897's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), −z facing south (bearing 200); the three arches are open. The building:parts the bake nests under the outline are also named outright (they go with it either way), so the nonbuildings check sees them claimed.

name: Le Triomphe de la République
note: Dalou's bronze group in the middle of the Place de la Nation, on its pedestal in a round basin. Standalone at the centre of OSM way 114877477 (historic=monument, not a building); −z faces west toward the Bastille, where the procession goes.

name: Barrière du Trône — Saint Louis
note: Ledoux's north column on the Cours de Vincennes (1787), Étex's Saint Louis on top (1845). Placed on OSM way 63638975's box (osmium, 2026-10-29).

name: Barrière du Trône — Philippe Auguste
note: Ledoux's south column, Dumont's Philippe Auguste on top. Placed on OSM way 77385192's box and its cross-shaped base (parts 285276897…900, 286455821/3; osmium, 2026-10-29). The building:parts the bake nests under the outline are also named outright (they go with it either way), so the nonbuildings check sees them claimed.

name: Le Lion de Belfort
note: Bartholdi's copper lion on the Place Denfert-Rochereau. Placed on its pedestal, OSM way 79629168's box turned to its long axis (osmium, 2026-10-29); the lion looks along local +x (bearing 209.5) — its real heading not checked against a photograph.

name: Fontaine Agam
note: Yaacov Agam's 1977 mosaic basin on the parvis: kerb, coloured bands in the floor, rows of jets. Fitted to OSM way 19464174 (osmium, local pbf). Low kerb only, so the dalle stays rideable round it.

name: Parvis de La Défense — paving
note: Decal of the dalle's paving from the Arche (local −x) to the Esplanade's east end: pink joint grid, red-pink strips along the axis, pink bands across. Axis and centre from the Arche (48.89256, 2.23577) at bearing 116, checked against Fontaine Agam on the line. Patterns read off the owner's Google satellite screenshot 2026-11-16 (approximate). defense-famous/parvis.ts.

name: Bassin Takis
note: Takis's 1988 pool of 49 signaux lumineux: steel stems 3-9 m with coloured lamps, standing in a dark basin. Fitted to OSM way 19463289 (osmium, local pbf). Low kerb only.

name: Grande Arche de la Défense
note: Spreckelsen and Andreu's hollow cube, 110.9 m (Wikipedia; soffit steps 100-108 m from OSM building:parts). Placed on OSM way 19441489's box (osmium, 2026-10-29), which carries the 6.33° twist; opening along local z, −z toward Paris. Faces plain per owner 2026-11-03: smooth marble outside, pale glass inside the opening, Grand Escalier 13 treads, Nuage, panoramic lifts. Outline, duplicate 621620714, roof way 225694316 and the ~30 parts are replaced.

name: Tour Montparnasse
note: The tower, on OSM way 16406633's box turned to its long axis (osmium, 2026-10-29): the bowed faces at local ±x, the notched ends at ±z, −z toward bearing 219.5. Named exactly as the skyline stand-in in tools/cities.ts, so the stand-in gives way to it within 1.3 km. `front` (not rotateDeg, which the skyline code would copy onto the stand-in, whose own frame is long on x while this model is long on z): the same turn, 39.5°, for the model.

name: Église Saint-Sulpice
note: Placed on OSM way 16077204's box turned to the church's axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the front (−z) to the Place Saint-Sulpice (bearing 262.6), the north tower at −x; the way and its building:parts are replaced. Tower tops Wikipedia's 73/68 m (OSM's tower parts stop at 58.4/56.4).

name: Église Saint-Eustache
note: OSM way 53762963 is tagged building=church AND building:part=yes with height=10, so the bake keeps a 10 m block and drops its parts (273063678…703: nave 40 m, towers 38/24): the model gives the body back. Placed on the way's box turned to the nave's own axis (osmium, 2026-10-30: bearing 99.2, on which OSM's cross-walls, piers and nave all agree), the west front (−z) at bearing 279.2, +x south. What the rider sees of the south transept and flank (rose, gallery, lancets, portal, round-arched tracery, flyers) is from the owner's street view from the Allée Jules-Supervielle; the positions of flyers and piers are OSM's; the dates and the architects of the west front are from memory.

name: Église de la Sainte-Trinité
note: Ballu's church at the head of the Chaussée-d'Antin. OSM way 49872150 has no parts or height (a flat block in the city); placed on its box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the front and tower (−z) to the square at bearing 163.9.

name: Église Saint-Roch
note: OSM way 42722202 has no parts or height; placed on its box turned to its long axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), local x along it with the front at −x on the Rue Saint-Honoré (bearing 216).

name: Église Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois
note: The church (way 53770908, a 20 m block in OSM) and Ballu's belfry beside it on the place (way 200452261, 50 m), both replaced and drawn together: placed on the church's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the porch (−x) facing the Louvre's colonnade (bearing 282.4), the belfry at local (−34, +29), outside the box. Its flank windows, rose, porch, flyers and balustrades are the Gothic kit's (monuments/gothic.ts), on the same plan; their tracery is generic and not surveyed from this church.

name: Église Saint-Germain-des-Prés
note: Placed on OSM way 62287173's box turned to the church's own axis (osmium, 2026-10-29: 6.5° off the footprint's minimum box), the tower (−z) to the west at bearing 285.7; the way and its building:parts (the tower 1461285707…717, which the city drew as a windowed block with its pinnacles floating over the roofs) are replaced. The Chapelle Saint-Symphorien (way 495635817) stays.

name: Église Saint-Augustin
note: Baltard's iron-framed church on the Boulevard Malesherbes. Placed on OSM way 67501490's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the front (−z) on the Place Saint-Augustin at bearing 155, the dome toward +z; the way (dropped by the bake) and its 20 building:parts nested under it (the dome drawn by the city as a flat-topped windowed tower, the turrets as box chimneys) are replaced. Heights follow the parts: drum and cap to 70, the red lantern to 83, the cross ~85.

name: Basilique Sainte-Clotilde
note: Gau and Ballu's neo-Gothic basilica over the Square Samuel-Rousseau. Placed on OSM way 64952290's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the front (−z) on the Parvis Maurice-Druon at bearing 25.9, the apse toward +z; the way and its building:parts nested under it (the towers drawn by the city as two flat-topped shafts) are replaced. Heights follow the parts: the nave's eaves 28.2 and ridge 37, the towers' octagonal spires 44.4–66, the crosses ~68.5.

name: Église Saint-Étienne-du-Mont
note: The Renaissance-fronted Gothic church beside the Panthéon. Placed on OSM way 55343672's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the front (−z) on the Place Sainte-Geneviève at bearing 283.7, +x south; the way and its ~80 building:parts nested under it (the front drawn by the city as a mansarded block, the belfry as a plain shaft) are replaced. Heights follow the parts: nave ridge 34.4, the belfry tower 46 and its dome and lantern to 53, the stair turret's cone 48. The church's south annex (way 255080058, building=church, inside the footprint along the south aisle and choir) goes with it; the Chapelle des Catéchismes (way 255080046) is OSM's and stays.

name: Église Saint-Séverin
note: The flamboyant church of the Latin Quarter. Placed on OSM way 19740659's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the west front (−z) at bearing 290.3, +x south; the way and its ~50 building:parts nested under it are replaced. Heights follow the parts: the aisles' gables ~12.5, the nave ridge 28.5, the tower 29.2 and its spire to 45.2.

name: Grande Mosquée de Paris
note: The Hispano-Moorish mosque on the Place du Puits-de-l'Ermite. Placed on the box of OSM relation 569853 (the complex's 1-level outline, which the bake keeps as a 4 m slab) turned to bearing 54.8 (osmium and the bake's rings, 2026-10-29); the relation and the standalone parts on it are replaced: way/320013175 is NOT the minaret but the prayer hall's green pyramid (5 levels + a 2-level pyramidal roof, roof:colour green), which the bake drew as a 28 m tower; the minaret is way/437776176 (27 m) with its lantern 437776174/5 to 33 (not in the bake). Drawn: the white enclosure coped in green tile, the institute and entrance ranges, the gate pavilion, the prayer hall and its pyramid to ~23, the patio with kiosks and fountain dome, the hammam dome, and the minaret to 33 with its jamur ~35.

name: Église Saint-Pierre de Montmartre
note: The village church of Montmartre beside the Sacré-Cœur. Placed on OSM way 23884336's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the west front (−z) on the Rue du Mont-Cenis at bearing 274.6, +x south; the way (dropped by the bake) and its ten building:parts nested under it (drawn by the city as a windowed block) are replaced. Heights follow the parts: the nave 16, the aisles 13, the bell tower 22 and its pyramid to 26.

name: Moulin de la Galette (Blute-Fin)
note: The Blute-Fin post mill (1622) in its garden between the Rue Lepic and the Rue Tholozé. Placed on OSM way 77780940 (8.2 m square; the city drew an 8 m box), the sails (−z) toward the Rue Lepic at bearing 190: the trestle tower, the weatherboarded body to ~13.4, the sails to ~19.

name: Moulin Radet
note: The Radet post mill on the corner of the Rue Lepic and the Rue Girardon. OSM's building:part 307906882 (tagged man_made=windmill, named 'Moulin de la Galette' with alt_name 'Moulin Radet') stands inside the restaurant's way 77780866 (4 m, which stays); the part is replaced by the model: a 4.4 m base under the mill, the body to ~12.4, the sails to ~16, turned toward the corner (bearing 150).

name: Église du Val-de-Grâce
note: Mansart's and Lemercier's domed church at the head of the Rue du Val-de-Grâce. Placed on OSM way 59846865's box turned to the church's axis (bearing 293, from the line of the portico's mapped columns; osmium, 2026-10-29), the front (−z) on the Place Alphonse-Laveran, the dome toward +z on x = −5.85; the way and its ~45 building:parts nested under it (the dome drawn by the city as a flat-topped octagonal shaft) are replaced. Heights follow the parts: the drum to 39.3 and its attic 43, the cap to 52.8, the lantern and spire to 62, the corner turrets 36.4, the portico's columns 14 and 26 and the pediment 30.2.

name: Église Saint-Vincent-de-Paul
note: Hittorff's basilica over the Place Franz-Liszt. Placed on OSM way 63197162's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the portico (−z) toward the place at bearing 190.3; the way (dropped by the bake) and its nine building:parts nested under it (towers and body drawn by the city as windowed blocks) are replaced. Heights follow the parts: the portico 20, the front between the towers 27.6, the nave 31, the towers 45. The stepped ramps on the place are OSM's steps, drawn by the city; the model's own 2.4 m terrace and steps stand inside the footprint.

name: Église Saint-François-Xavier
note: The neo-Renaissance church on the Place du Président-Mithouard. Placed on OSM way 68893289's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the front (−z) on the Boulevard des Invalides at bearing 54.6, the apse toward +z; OSM has no parts (8 levels, drawn by the city as a 32 m flat block). Heights from the photographs against the 29 m front: the pediment ~28, the towers' crosses ~43, the crossing dome's lantern ~46.

name: Chapelle expiatoire
note: Percier and Fontaine's domed chapel and its walled garden in the Square Louis-XVI. Placed on the box of the precinct (OSM relation 1068013, which the bake drew as a 20 m block round a hole) turned to the chapel's axis (osmium and the bake's rings, 2026-10-29), the portico facing the garden (−z, bearing 84.6); the relation and the chapel (way 67557301, a 20 m box in the city) are replaced: the cenotaph galleries down both sides, the porter's pavilion at the far end, the chapel's terrace, Doric portico, vestibule, trefoil of half-domed apses and the green dome and lantern to ~19.5.

name: Grande Synagogue de la Victoire
note: Aldrophe's great synagogue on the Rue de la Victoire. Placed on OSM way 69363730's box (osmium, 2026-10-29), the front (−z) toward the Rue de la Victoire at bearing 181 (the street runs ~10 m south of it, past the forecourt railings); OSM has no parts (the city drew a 28 m flat block). The central bay's great arch to 36 m (Wikipedia), the nave's roof to 33, the ranges round it to 18.

name: Cathédrale de la Sainte-Trinité
note: Wilmotte's Russian cathedral on the Quai Branly (2016). Placed on OSM way 449077939's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the door and three slits on the Avenue Rapp at bearing 79 (Mapillary; the other three faces by symmetry); the way (height 24) and its five `onion` parts are replaced. To 37 m at the cross (Wikipedia). The Centre Culturel and the parish centre beside it stay the city's.

name: Cathédrale Saint-Alexandre-Nevsky
note: The Russian cathedral of the Rue Daru (Kouzmine and Strohm, 1861). Placed on OSM way 70192893's box turned square to its arms (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the porch toward the Rue Daru at bearing 319; the way (height 6, as a mansard) and its five pyramidal parts are replaced. Central tent to 48 m at the cross (OSM's part, Wikipedia); small towers from OSM's rings, heights read off Commons photographs (OSM's 24 is short of them).

name: Fontaine Stravinsky
note: Tinguely and Saint Phalle's sixteen works in the basin between the Pompidou, the IRCAM and Saint-Merri (1983). Centred on OSM way 88301107's box (natural=water, height 0.75; osmium, 2026-10-30), its long axis along z, +z toward the IRCAM at bearing 28. The kerb is OSM's ring; the works' places are from Commons photographs and memory, not a survey.

name: Arènes de Lutèce
note: Roman Paris's amphitheatre between the Rue Monge and the Rue de Navarre. Centred on OSM way 406229046's box (historic=archaeological_site, 81 × 65 m; osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the stage toward bearing 80; the size is the arena proper, so that the box clears only the arena and not the houses and the square's trees round it (the model's stage, tiers and passages reach out past it); the two `building=ruins` ways, which the city would raise as buildings, are replaced. Walls, passages and the stage wall are OSM's rings, the tiers follow the Gradins ways. Heights are read off Commons photographs; the game's ground has no bowl here, so the floor is at ground level and the tiers rise from it, with a grass bank behind.

name: Mémorial des Martyrs de la Déportation
note: Pingusson's memorial at the tip of the Île de la Cité (1962). Placed on OSM relation 9396191's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the prow toward bearing 122, the relation (building=yes, layer 1) replaced; its outer ring and hole are the wedge and the court. The two stairs are from photographs, not mapped. The real court lies 3–4 m below the garden and the game's ground cannot be dug: the terrace is raised about 1.35 m above the lawn, the court's floor is at the ground, and the whole follows the ground (`drape`), which falls toward the island's tip.

name: Église Saint-Jean de Montmartre
note: De Baudot's church of brick, ceramic and reinforced cement on the Place des Abbesses (1904). Placed on OSM way 77807770's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the portal toward bearing 42; the way is replaced. The walls are its ring, the front from one Commons elevation, heights read off it (OSM has only five levels); sides and back not checked against a photograph.

name: Mur des Fédérés
note: The Communards' wall in Père-Lachaise's south-east corner (Wikidata Q910923). Placed on OSM's plaque node 5220080010, the wall's centre line along way 13859706 (bearing 64.5), the plaque facing the cemetery side toward bearing 334.5 (osmium, 2026-11-22). Wall ~2.9 m, plaque ~2.3 x 1.45 m, the paved court and beds are estimated from two Commons photographs against the plaque, not surveyed; the ivy and plantings are stand-ins. No sculpture: no Modly piece.

name: Monument aux fusillés de la Cascade
note: Memorial to the 16 young Resistance men shot by the Grande Cascade, 16 Aug 1944 (Wikidata Q3091182). Placed on OSM's memorial node 4484420031. A round stele ~2.4 m with two crosses, in a ring of green mesh fence with two flower bowls, scaled by eye off Commons photographs, not surveyed; the front bearing 270 (toward the track 8 m west) is a guess. No sculpture: no Modly piece.

name: Mémorial de la Shoah
note: The memorial on the Rue Geoffroy-l'Asnier. Placed on the box of OSM's museum polygon (way 124052479; osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the street at bearing 122; the main block (way 55620205) and the street front (way 55620119, building=roof) are replaced, their rings OSM's. The street front is from one Commons photograph; the court and the block's front are from memory and not confirmed by one.

name: Église Notre-Dame-de-Lorette
note: Lebas's Roman basilica closing the Rue Laffitte (1836). Placed on OSM way 25688622's box in its own axis (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the portico at bearing 193; the way is replaced. Heights from Commons photographs (OSM gives ten levels); the belfry's place on the left flank from one of them.

name: Chapelle Saint-Louis de la Salpêtrière
note: Bruant's octagonal chapel of the Salpêtrière (1677). Placed on OSM way 78535716's box turned to its main arm (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z at bearing 334: the widest arm, toward the Boulevard de l'Hôpital's gate and opposite OSM's `Abside` (way 377136988, bearing 157); no photograph of that front was found, so the choice of arm is inferred. The way and the 14 parts inside it are replaced. The octagon and lantern from OSM's parts (to 32 and 40), the drum and dome's split from Commons photographs. The main porch is from memory.

name: Tour Jean-sans-Peur
note: The keep of the Hôtel de Bourgogne (1411), Rue Étienne-Marcel. On OSM node 250657151 (height 27); stands within the school's own outline (relation 550212), which is not claimed. Its size, stages and the rubble wall from two Commons photographs; its bearing from the school's plan.

name: Église Saint-Ambroise
note: Ballu's twin-spired church on the Boulevard Voltaire (1868). Placed on OSM way 63638108's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the portals at bearing 235; the way is replaced. Walls from its ring, the front from one Commons photograph, spires to 68 m (Wikipedia); nave and apse above the walls not checked.

name: Église Saint-Laurent
note: The Gothic church by the Gare de l'Est, its west front of 1866. Placed on OSM way 63200612's box in its own axis (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the portal at bearing 270; the way and the three parts inside it are replaced. The front and tower from one Commons photograph from the south-west; the tower's side and all heights are estimated from it.

name: Église Saint-Nicolas-des-Champs
note: The wide Gothic church on the Rue Saint-Martin. Placed on OSM way 56290843's box in its own axis (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the door at bearing 291; the way and the two parts inside it are replaced. Walls from its ring (the front runs 6.6° off square), front, tower and south flank from a Commons photograph; heights read off it; north side and choir not checked.

name: Fontaine de Varsovie
note: The long basin of the Jardins du Trocadéro (1937). Centred on OSM way 79738429's box (natural=water; osmium, 2026-10-30), −z down the axis at bearing 134; the kerb and water are its ring, without its side channels, and follow the ground. The twenty cannons, side jets and plumes are placed by their reported pattern, not surveyed, and stand still. The size is the pool, not the head's cross-basin, so that it does not clear the garden's trees either side.

name: Fontaine du Palmier
note: The column of 1808 and its palm-leaf capital on the Place du Châtelet, the gilt Victory, Boizot's four allegories, the four sphinxes (Wikipedia fr). Centred on OSM way 261092850 (building=yes, 9.9 × 10 m, the upper basin), which is replaced; the frame along that way's edges at bearing 23/113. Four-square, so `front` matters little. Heights and the kerb's radius by proportion from a Commons elevation scaled on OSM's 10 m: the reference gave no height in metres.

name: Fontaine Saint-Sulpice
note: Visconti's fountain of the four bishops on the Place Saint-Sulpice: three octagonal basins, four lions, four vases, the square shrine with Bossuet to the north (Wikipedia fr, which gives 12 m; the Commons photograph scaled on the first basin is nearer 14). Centred on OSM way 40068036's octagonal kerb (amenity=fountain, 22 m across its flats); front −z north, along the flat at bearing 352. Tiers and proportions from two Commons photographs.

name: Fontaine des Quatre-Saisons
note: Bouchardon's palace front at 57–59 rue de Grenelle. OSM way 64952163 (an unnamed building=yes, replaced) is the arc of the wall itself, 3 m deep, and the node 1687173492 carries the name; the wall's arc (radius 22 m, concave to the street) and the block on its centre are measured from that way and mirrored about the block, because the west half is mapped only in part in its neighbours' outlines. Front −z faces the street at bearing 33 (osmium: the wall is on the street's south side). Wikipedia fr gives about ten metres high and nearly twenty wide; OSM's outline reads about 29 wide. Elevation from three Commons photographs.

name: Fontaine du Château-d'Eau
note: Davioud's fountain, moved in 1880 from what is now the Place de la République to the Place Félix-Éboué (Wikipedia fr). Centred on OSM way 78008833 (natural=water, 29.7 m across). Steps, tazzas and the pairs of bronze lions on their piers from a Commons photograph and an old print: the number and placing of the lions is read from those, not a text.

name: Statue de la Liberté — Île aux Cygnes
note: The bronze at the downstream tip of the island. OSM node 465294103 (height 11.5). Sources agree she was turned toward the west in 1937; the bearing, 228, is taken along the island's own footway, not measured. The figure, the gilt flame and the tablet's two dates from a Commons photograph; the pedestal by eye, no source for its height found.

name: Hautes Herbes
note: Béatrice Guichard, 2003: eight steel blades of grass, some with a gilt edge, rising from the gravel of the Place du Louvre before Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois. OSM node 8458628895. The blades read from a Commons photograph (Hautes Herbes.jpg, Aquilae); heights, bends and turns by eye, tunable in hautes-herbes.ts. The sand under it is the city's own (an OSM area); the builder's disc is off (DRAW_SAND). The Tripo route failed: too thin to photograph.

name: Monument du Maréchal Moncey
note: Doublemard's bronze on Guillaume's pedestal (1869), 14 m (Wikipedia fr), the middle of the Place de Clichy. Centred on OSM way 68247750 (historic=memorial, round, 7.3 m). Group and pedestal from a Commons photograph. The bearing is a guess, up the Avenue de Clichy: no source for which way the group faces was found.

name: Monument à Pasteur
note: Falguière's monument, finished by Peter and Dubois, on the Place de Breteuil (Wikipedia fr). Centred on OSM way 238841686, the square of its plinth, and standing in the ring of 39 m the bake found, so the generic place monument gives way. The lawn's radius is the ring's less the road, as in render/paris/roundabout-monuments.ts. Figures placed roughly, from two Commons photographs. Bearing 184 read off one of them, not confirmed.

name: George Washington — Place d'Iéna
note: French and Potter's bronze, dedicated 3 July 1900, the sword raised. OSM node 570349020, at the centre of the ring of 21 m the bake found, so the generic place monument gives way. Pedestal and pose from a 1913 autochrome on Commons; the bearing, up the Avenue d'Iéna, is read from the same picture's background and not confirmed.

name: CNIT
note: The vault of 1958 (Camelot, de Mailly, Zehrfuss; Prouvé; reglazed 2009): triangle of 218 m a side on three abutments (OSM relation 3071527 and parts, all replaced), 46.3 m at the crown (Wikipedia fr, matching the 46 m BD TOPO apex). Three corrugated shell lobes meeting in valleys to the corners, white rim, inclined glass arches with vertical fins, Hilton/office blocks inside. Shape from Commons photos: Puteaux - Centre des nouvelles industries et technologies - 2025-10-08 17-14-11 001.jpg and 2010-09-28 - CNIT Paris 22.jpg.

name: Tour First
note: KPF 2011 rebuild of Tour UAP: Y plan of three wings (NW 231 m, E 190 m, S 170 m, each with a 25 m sloped glass screen), core crown and mast to 259 m, 16 m glass atrium base. Plan and part heights from OSM parts (osmium, local pbf); look from Commons 'Tour First - La Defense - Inauguration 6 mai 2011.jpg'. Lidar not measured.

name: Les 4 Temps
note: Westfield Les 4 Temps: OSM way 396802664's outline (defense-famous/quatreTemps.ts). Glazed shopfronts on the parvis faces, glass entrance with the red Westfield band and sloped glass canopy at the top of the steps (OSM flights, 48.89142,2.2365), roof car-park decks at the east end. Generic OSM buildings inside the footprint claimed (osmium, 2026-11-16). Roof height by eye over the parvis.

name: Dôme Imax
note: The glass ball by the Grande Arche: OSM part way 186981683, named, 38 m across and height 27. Its grid of panes from the same Commons photograph as Le Dôme's.

name: L'Araignée Rouge
note: Calder's Grand Stabile Rouge: OSM way 186981704 (height 15), which is replaced. Its silhouette traced from one Commons photograph; the cross plates from memory. Which side of it faces bearing 206 was not checked against the outline.

name: Le Pouce
note: César's bronze thumb, height 12 and 4.4 × 4.5 m from OSM way 186981693, which is replaced. No usable photograph was fetched: the shape is simply a thumb's, and the bearing, nail side toward 206, is a guess.

name: Fers
note: Driss Sans-Arcidet's monument to General Dumas (2009), OSM node 7952476083. Shape and sizes by eye from Commons 'Unchained (64188317).jpeg': tall ring with broken chain, cuff with hanging chain; bearing a guess.

name: Monument des Droits de l'Homme
note: Jantzen and Theimer's mastaba-like tower of 1989 in the Champ de Mars (Wikidata Q3323344). Placed on the centre of OSM way 369434380 (a 14.5 m square podium turned 45 deg; osmium, 2026-11-22), the front (−z) the south-west face toward the Champ de Mars at bearing 225, the bronze door on the back. Podium from OSM; the tower (~7.2 m wide, 12 m tall), the two bronze obelisks (~14.5 m) and the figures' places are scaled off one wide photograph against the figures, not surveyed; the seals, triangle and sundial are stand-ins. The figures are Modly models (statues manifest: droits-group, droits-toga).

name: Fontaine Louvois
note: Visconti's cast-iron fountain of 1844 in the square Louvois (Wikidata Q3076038; sculptor Klagmann): octagonal basin (OSM way 26277959, ~6 m flat to centre, a sloppy polygon so +-1 m; vertices near east, hence front 25), square pedestal with four tritons on dolphins, a wide bowl with zodiac band and mascarons, an upper pedestal, the four river goddesses back to back under the top bowl. Basin from OSM; bowls, pedestals and the ~8.5 m total height scaled off Commons photographs against the 3.6 m goddess group, not surveyed. Goddesses and top bowl are a Modly model (statues manifest: louvois-group), the tritons likewise (louvois-triton).

name: Fontaine de la Paix (Détournelle)
note: Détournelle's stone pylon fountain of 1806-10 in the allée du Séminaire off the rue Bonaparte (Wikidata Q3076202, monument historique 1926, reliefs by Voinier, Espercieux, Caraffe, Marquois): a plinth, a die with garland frieze and a pediment on each long face, four relief panels (A LA PAIX, SCIENCES ET ARTS, AGRICULTURE, COMMERCE), a mascaron and shell bowl on each long face, in a rectangular trough. Trough 5.3 x 3.8 m from OSM way 1200013023 (centre taken from it); the pylon's ~1.8 x 1.2 m die and ~5.2 m height scaled off Commons photographs against the trough, not surveyed. Reliefs are drawn as shallow dark panels (procedural, no Modly pieces). Which long face is the front (bearing) is a guess from the photos.

name: La Danse de la fontaine émergente
note: Chen Zhen's 2008 dragon-fountain on the place Augusta-Holmès (Wikidata Q747835; OSM node 447873149 is a point, no footprint to claim): a row of glass tubes with water inside breaking the paving, ringed with steel hoops and crested with scalloped steel fins. Procedural only (monument-kit sweptTube/hoop/finPlate). Hump count (5), length (~30 m), height (~2.1 m) and the serpentine are read off ONE Commons photo (Place_Augusta_Holmes_03) against a car and lamp post, not surveyed; orientation (front 0) is a guess: check against an aerial. The head is not visible in the photo, so the body just dives under at both ends. No Modly part: nothing figurative survives.

name: Fontaine Molière
note: Visconti's wall fountain of 1844 at the corner of rue de Richelieu and rue Molière (Wikidata Q3076047; Seurre's bronze Molière, Pradier's two Muses): a shell-headed niche between pairs of Corinthian columns, entablature dated MDCCCXLIV, an arched pediment, the dedication pedestal, a stepped basin. Claims OSM way 54097804 (the fountain mapped as a building, ~8.3 m across the back, back wall on its SW edge, front toward the place Mireille at bearing 39). Heights (~12 m) and the 2.4 m seated bronze scaled off Commons photographs, not surveyed; the tympanum relief is a stand-in. Molière and the Muses are Modly models (statues manifest: moliere-seated, moliere-muse-1, moliere-muse-2).

name: Fontaine Gaillon
note: Visconti's wall fountain of 1828 on the south face of the corner house in the place Gaillon (Wikidata Q579833): shell-headed niche between two Corinthian columns, entablature, attic with the MDCCCXXVII dedication and two urns, two-tier basin on balusters, a putto on a dolphin on the upper bowl (Modly, gaillon-dauphin). The host house (OSM way 54531802, apartments) is NOT claimed; the model starts at its south face (y 949.3 in the paris-centre frame), centred on its middle (x 169.1). Dimensions are scaled off two Commons photos against column spacing ~4 m, not surveyed; lower rim ~1.5 m is the shakiest figure.

name: Fontaine du Vert Bois
note: The 1712 wall fountain of the rue Saint-Martin / rue du Vertbois (Wikidata Q3076291): a stone portal against the foot of the Saint-Martin-des-Champs tower, rusticated pilasters, relief, bronze plaque, shell and bronze mascaron spout, cornice and a cartouche of arms on top (Modly: vertbois-crown, vertbois-mascaron). OSM way 54964126 (amenity=fountain) claimed. Faces the rue Saint-Martin / rue du Vertbois junction (front 335, NNW), the tower to its right: read off OSM's footway/fence line and the junction position, not checked on site. Dimensions scaled off Commons photos at ~80 px/m (pilaster ~0.9 m), not surveyed; heights shakiest.

name: Fontaine Childebert
note: The Childebert (abbaye Saint-Germain) wall fountain of 1715-17 re-erected in the square Paul-Langevin (Wikidata Q3076004): ashlar pier with pilasters, shell niche, sunk panel, shelf, bronze mascaron (Modly) and a low curved basin, against the trellised terrace wall. Position: the Commons geotag (48.84768, 2.35025) moved ~3.5 m SW to the foot of the terrace wall seen in the game; front and dimensions estimated from photos (not surveyed). No OSM way mapped for it.

name: Fontaine Dejean
note: Formigé's fountain of 1906 (Q3076013, OSM node 2482248710) in the square de la place Pasdeloup beside the Cirque d'Hiver: octagonal base with carved frieze, two scallop shells, gadrooned bowl, tapering shaft with Dejean's oval portrait medallion and inscription, acanthus vase and sphere under a pelican (Modly, dejean-pelican). No OSM way to claim (a node). Heights and widths are scaled off Commons photos against the medallion (~0.4 m) and base (~1 m across), not surveyed; the facing (medallion to the south) is a guess.

name: Fontaine de Jarente
note: The 1783 stone pavilion closing the impasse de la Poissonnerie off the rue de Jarente (Wikidata Q1435786), 4.7 m wide like OSM's end wall (the host houses are OSM ways 56045039 / 1174634452, not claimed; the model stands 0.6 m in front of their face). Rusticated pilasters, entablature, pediment with a shell cartouche, stepped pyramid roof, cartouche panel, plain tablet, mask spout and trough, all procedural (the cartouche is shallow relief: no Modly piece). Dimensions scaled off Commons photographs against the side doors and the OSM wall width, not surveyed; roof heights are guessed; front bearing 207 read from the end wall's normal.

name: Fontaine du Marché-aux-Carmes
note: Fragonard's herm fountain of 1830, moved to the square Gabriel-Pierné (rue de Seine / rue Mazarine, 6e) in 1930 (Wikidata Q3076266; the old Marché des Carmes was at place Maubert, but the fountain stands here, at the list's coordinates). Basin radius 1.32 m from OSM way 1200620877 (claimed); pillar 0.64 x 0.46 m, 2.5 m to the shoulders, spouts at 1.0 m, scaled off three Commons photos against the basin width, not surveyed. The two-faced head with its fruit-basket crown is a Modly model (carmes-head), made from one face's photos so only one face is real; the bust fronts on the pillar are flat stand-ins.

name: Fontaine du Château d'eau de Montmartre
note: Titeux's wall fountain of 1835 on the front of the old Montmartre reservoir (9b rue Norvins, Wikidata Q945052; OSM way 77937860, the disused reservoir building, claimed: ring extruded as the body, front on its SSW edge, bearing 197). Aedicule 5 m wide, ~7.2 m to the pediment, 8-step stair, niche 2.6 m wide, scaled off two Commons photos against the niche and stair, not surveyed; pink marble panels and the frieze are flat stand-ins. The bronze vase with dolphin feet in the niche is a Modly model (reservoir-vase).

name: Fontaine aux Lions de Nubie
note: Girard's fountain of 1811 (fontaine du Château d'eau, Q3076267) in the Place de la Fontaine-aux-Lions, La Villette; OSM way 81752247 (a 0.6 m wall outline, ~26 m across, claimed). Pool, two round steps, four diagonal piers, core and two-tazza plume are by eye from Commons photographs (Fontaine Château Eau Pierre Simon Girard Paris 1-4): radii and heights are guesses, only the 26 m outline is measured. The eight cast-iron lions (two a pier) are Modly pieces attached from paris-statues.json at LION_AT.

name: Fontaine du puits de Grenelle
note: The fountain of 1906 (Q3076301) in the round planter of place Georges-Mulot, 15e, on the site of the first artesian well; OSM way 252282895 (natural=water, the 3.4 m planter circle) claimed. Square ashlar shaft with four engaged corner columns, plinth, oval medallions on the four faces, cornice, stepped stone cap and ball. Heights and widths are scaled off the Commons photo 'Fontaine du Puits de Grenelle.jpg' against the mascaron (~0.33 m) and plinth (~2.1 m), not surveyed; medallions/frames are shallow relief kept procedural. The bronze mascaron (south face) is a procedural stand-in: three Modly attempts (hunyuan21, trellis2 x2) from the only usable photo (~140 px of face) gave flat slabs, so none is published.

name: Monument à Gavarni
note: Denys Puech and Henri Guillaume's monument of 1904 (Q3076026, OSM node tagged amenity=fountain) in the middle of the place Saint-Georges roundabout: iron railing, round basin, square plinth with a bronze mask on two sides, a stout round column carrying Gavarni's carnival figures in high relief, frieze, cornice and the half-length statue of Gavarni. Dimensions scaled by eye off Commons photos (Monument Gavarni 2021-06-27 -3/-5, Fontaine Gavarni Paris 9e) against the railing (~1 m); about 7.4 m in all, not surveyed. Which way the front faces is a guess (-z). No OSM building ways under it.

name: Fontaine du Bassin Soufflot
note: Davioud's basin (1862) in the place Edmond-Rostand, 6e, with Crauk's bronze Triton and nereid holding a shell (Q3076290; OSM way 685770760, fountain+water+wall height 0.5, ring radius ~7 m measured). Rim width, the 8 support blocks and the ring of small jets are by eye off Commons photos; the group is Modly soufflot-triton.

name: Fontaine des Ambassadeurs
note: Hittorff's fountain of 1840 in the jardins des Champs-Elysees (Q3076221; OSM way 67091995, amenity=fountain + water, 5.6 m across, measured): low round stone basin, square panelled pedestal, reed-and-mask cluster, wide cast-iron bowl with eight mascarons spilling into the basin, bronze nymph on top (Modly ambassadeurs-nymphe). Every height and the bowl and pedestal widths are by eye off Commons photos (Fontaine des Ambassadeurs Paris 8e 001/003) against the basin wall, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine de la Petite-Halle
note: Beausire's free-standing ashlar fountain pavilion of 1719 at the rue du Faubourg-Saint-Antoine / rue de Montreuil (Q3076204, also Fontaine de Montreuil; OSM way 63649496, claimed, 4.5 x 5.2 m with its niche dent). Stepped plinth, corner pilasters, cornice, pediment on each face, hipped roof; arched niche with trough and the bearded bronze mascaron (Modly montreuil-mascaron); blind arches/oculi on the sides, a door at the back. Heights, which face is which and the door side read off two Commons photos against the door (~2 m), not surveyed.

name: Miroir d'eau, la Seine et ses affluents
note: Raoul Larche's fountain of 1900-1901 in the square Jean-Perrin beside the Grand Palais (Q3076034): a lobed oval marble basin with the Seine and her tributaries seated on its rim. Plan = OSM ways 66758129 (outer) and 66758138 (water), measured; rim height 0.6 m and group sizes by eye against Commons photos. The sculpture groups are Modly pieces in paris-statues.json.

name: Bassin rond du Petit Palais (sud)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (Q2887588; south-east round basin at the foot of the avenue Winston-Churchill, Petit Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66768636, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin rond du Grand Palais (sud)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (Q2887588; south-west round basin, Grand Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66755254, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin rond du Grand Palais (nord)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (north-west round basin, Grand Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66755262, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin rond du Petit Palais (nord)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (north-east round basin, Petit Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66768651, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin ovale du Petit Palais (Champs-Élysées)
note: The oval basin on the Champs-Élysées promenade east of the avenue Winston-Churchill (OSM way 66768655, 11.7 x 8 m measured; its west twin is the next entry; Larche's Miroir d'eau is a separate basin). Vase bowl, jet and the small bronze dolphins are procedural stand-ins by eye off Commons (Bassin du Grand Palais 5): Modly not attempted.

name: Bassin ovale du Grand Palais (square de Berlin)
note: The oval basin on the Champs-Élysées promenade west of the avenue Winston-Churchill, Grand Palais side (OSM way 66768634, 11.5 x 7.8 m measured, rim 0.5 tagged; not the Miroir d'eau, which is Larche's separate basin in square Jean-Perrin). Vase bowl, jet and small bronze dolphins are procedural stand-ins by eye off Commons (Bassin du Grand Palais 5): Modly not attempted.

name: L'Embâcle (Daudelin, place du Québec)
note: Charles Daudelin's 1984 fountain-sculpture in the place du Québec (Q3076308): bronze plates tilted up out of the paving round a shallow pool. All procedural (src/render/landmarks/paris/monuments/minor/fontaine-embacle.ts, kit tiltedSlab). Position and pool footprint from OSM way 664223075 (the Wikidata/list coordinate 48.85330,2.33306 is ~28 m south, inside an apartment block, so it was not used). Plate count, tilts, sizes and the ~1.6 m peak are by eye off two Commons photos, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine de Joyeuse
note: Boitel's stone edicule of 1847 at 41 rue de Turenne (Q3076142, also Fontaine Saint-Louis): fluted pilasters on pedestals, entablature with the arms of Paris, archivolt over a semi-domed niche, iron grille, lobed tazza over a half-round basin, the zinc child with a jar (Modly joyeuse-enfant). Real one is recessed into the house; here it stands about 1 m proud, its back 0.55 m in front of the house face (OSM building ways at x about 2369.7 not claimed; the face line and its 92 degree normal read off the OSM polygon, so the model centre is 1 m east of it). Width ~3.3 m from frwiki (about 3 m) and photos; heights scaled against a scooter, not surveyed.

name: Monument aux soldats noirs morts pour la France
note: Stele in the Jardin d'agronomie tropicale (Q17745972, OSM memorial node, memorial=stele; Wikidata gives 48.8332 2.4661): a pale stone slab with a bas-relief of a woman beside a Poilu's helmet, on an inscribed die, three steps and a low wing wall each side. Placed on the OSM node; facing south (away from the Pavillon de l'Indochine, per the 1900s postcard) is a guess. Dimensions by eye off Commons photographs (die ~2 m wide), not surveyed. The woman is Modly soldatsnoirs-femme (paris-statues.json).

name: Monument à Komitas
note: Bronze Komitas by David Erevantsi (2003, Q3323366) on a plain limestone cube at the west end of the Cours Albert-1er, placed on Wikidata's coordinates (no OSM building there). Pedestal ~1.6 x 1.4 x 1.5 m and statue ~2.8 m estimated off Commons photos, not surveyed; the inscription face toward the south is a guess. The statue is Modly komitas-statue (paris-statues.json).

name: Monument aux morts du Père-Lachaise
note: Bartholome's war memorial (1899, Q3323309; OSM way 311412497, width 14.1, height 8): a limestone mausoleum front at the top of the Avenue Principale steps, doorway with the couple (Modly pere-couple), a mourning group each side (pere-gauche, pere-droite), the sunk panel of the dead (shallow, procedural), bronze wing doors with step flights. Placed at the OSM polygon's long front edge (osmium; facing bearing 241.9, down the steps). Dimensions scaled by eye off Commons photographs against the 14.1 m OSM width, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine du Cirque
note: Hittorff and Barre's cast-iron fountain of 1839 in the jardins des Champs-Elysees (Wikidata Q3076259, OSM way 67036988 whose water ring is only ~3 m radius): wide low round stone basin (~8.3 m across by eye off Commons photos, a bench and people as scale), octagonal pedestal, big bowl with twelve lion mascarons, the four Seasons (children) back to back under a smaller bowl with dog and wolf heads. Sizes are estimates, not surveyed. The children group is a Modly model (statues manifest: cirque-saisons).

name: Fontaine de Diane
note: Hittorff's fountain of 1840 (Q3076128; also fontaine Ledoyen) in the jardin des Champs-Élysées, sister of the Cirque, Ambassadeurs and Grille du Coq fountains (kit routine hittorffFountain). Basin radius 3.0 m from OSM way 1136105125 (claimed); wall, octagonal pedestal, neck, vasque (~3.7 m across), 12 lion-mask lugs and reed tuft are by eye off Commons photos 'Fontaine de Diane Paris 8e 001-003', not surveyed. Desprez's Diane (~1.8 m) is Modly diane-diane.

name: Fontaine de la Grille du Coq
note: Hittorff's fountain of 1840 (Q3076190) facing the Grille du Coq of the Elysee garden, the one sister of Diane/Cirque/Ambassadeurs with no sculpture (kit hittorffFountain with a plain jet). Position and 3.0 m basin radius from OSM way 67092064 (claimed); Wikidata/frwiki coordinates (48.8674, 2.3180) just copy the Ambassadeurs fountain and are wrong. Pedestal, neck, vasque and jet sizes copy the sister fountains, by eye, not surveyed. No Modly piece.

name: Fontaine du Théâtre-Français — Nymphe marine
note: Davioud's twin fountains of 1872-74 in the place André-Malraux (1er), one drawing for both (src/render/landmarks/paris/monuments/minor/fontaine-theatre-francais.ts). Basin width measured from the OSM way (amenity=fountain + water + wall, 11.3 m across); every height, the bowls and the column are by eye off Commons photos (2026-08 set, Fontaine Nymphe Marine / Fluviale Paris 2, 5, 9). Nymphe marine with an oar by Carrier-Belleuse (Q3076333) and four seated putti by Eude: Modly pieces theatre-marine-nymphe, theatre-marine-putti.

name: Fontaine du Théâtre-Français — Nymphe fluviale
note: Davioud's twin fountains of 1872-74 in the place André-Malraux (1er), one drawing for both (src/render/landmarks/paris/monuments/minor/fontaine-theatre-francais.ts). Basin width measured from the OSM way (amenity=fountain + water + wall, 11.3 m across); every height, the bowls and the column are by eye off Commons photos (2026-08 set, Fontaine Nymphe Marine / Fluviale Paris 2, 5, 9). Winged Nymphe fluviale with a reed by Moreau and four seated putti by Gauthier: Modly pieces theatre-fluviale-nymphe, theatre-fluviale-putti.
